chunks: for I, while hesitating in my reply to you and listening to your letter, have had my view weakened and my intuition erring.

And indeed, when you refer your demands to me and expect me to send you written replies, you are like one who is in deep slumber while his dreams contradict him, or one who stands perplexed and overwhelmed, not knowing whether whatever comes to him is for him or against him.
You are not such a man but he is (to some extent) like you (as you are worse than him).

key_terms.الْمُسْتَثْقِلِ: The one who is heavy-laden or in deep slumber

ai.seo_question: What metaphors did Ali use to describe Muawiya's state of confusion in his letter?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi’s compilation places this letter in the context of the political tension preceding the Battle of Siffin, where Ali (AS) reflects on the psychological burden of engaging with Muawiya’s persistent yet often ambiguous demands. The metaphors of the sleeper and the overwhelmed standing man highlight not just confusion, but the strategic difficulty of responding to a rival who shifts positions to suit his political aims, a theme central to Shia political thought regarding legitimacy and patience. This passage underscores the Imam’s introspective state as he weighs the wisdom of continued correspondence against the inevitability of conflict.

en.sayed-ali-raza: (in) exchanging replies and listening to your letters my view has been weak and my intelligence has been erring.

When you refer your demands to me and expect me to send you written replies, you are like one who is in deep slumber while his dreams contradict him, or one who stands perplexed and overwhelmed, not knowing whether whatever comes to him is for him or against him.
You are not such a man but he is (to some extent) like you (as you are worse than him).
